title: Microservices vs monoliths

kcs.statement: Microservices split an application into independently deployable services, each owning its own data and communicating over the network through APIs or messages.
Microservices buy independent scaling and deployment at the cost of network latency, partial failures, distributed transactions and harder debugging, so a monolith is often the right starting point.
Services that share one database or must be deployed together form a distributed monolith: they carry the costs of distribution without the independence.
